title: I'm a microbiology graduate and I made an incremental game about microscopic life in a petri dish: Welcome to Petri. (Free, browser and windows available)
author: No_Ticket_5074
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/qmnkk1j4eozh1.gif

* Amoebae hunt down and digest stray bacteria.
* Slime mould grows a vein network between its colonies and your media.
* Yeast buds and cyanobacteria give off oxygen bubbles.
* Phages land on a colony and burst its cells until you pop them.

Systems: tiered upgrades and synergies, 7 different media, a branching Gene Lab with either/or choices, CRISPR edits you can see in the dish, mutations, grant proposals, six vessels from a Petri dish to an entire biosphere, two separate layers of prestiging, three lineages that change how a run is played, four challenge modes, and I even remembered to put an ending in, how thoughtful I am :)  


* The full game takes somewhere between 50-80 hours to complete at a relaxed pace, with offline progress.
* Mouse only controls, saves automatically, and save export/import.
* **AI disclosure**

Petri was built with Claude (Anthropic’s AI assistant) as a coding partner.

* **Code:** most of the code was written by Claude, directed, playtested and reviewed by me.
* **Art:** the organism art, vessels and textures are drawn procedurally by code Claude wrote; no image-generation models were used.
* **Sound:** all sound is synthesised at runtime by code Claude wrote; no AI audio models.
* **Text:** the in-game text (organism descriptions, Lab Notes, the store page) was drafted with Claude from my notes and hand-edited by me.
* **Design and science:** the game design, balance targets and the microbiology are from me.

I'd love feedback on pacing in particular: where the game feels like it starts to drag, where things go a bit off the rails and are too fast, and anywhere that it's unclear where to go next. Also if you are a fellow microbiologist and feel like something looks wrong, tell me so I can get it fixed ASAP!

This game is a side project while I work on a much more realistic microscopic evolution sim and is mostly just meant to be a fun, less intense version of that, if there are any computational biologists who are interested in seeing the progress I have made on a more realistic simulation with the goal of having digital microbes evolve glycolysis from fragmented genes let me know and I can find the right place to talk about that as well! :D

Hope you all enjoy the game, please leave me any suggestions for additions or changes in the comments!
